newsitem.title: CHINA: Nestle sees China sales doubling.
newsitem.headline: Nestle sees China sales doubling.

text.p: Nestle SA, the Swiss food giant, expects total investment in China to reach five billion yuan ($602 million) by 2000 and to double its sales every two years, chairman Helmut Maucher said on Thursday.

Nestle had so far completed nine of 11 projects planned in its initial 2.8 billion yuan investment in China and expected sales in China, not including Hong Kong, of 1.5 billion yuan in 1996, company officials said.
Nestle's businesses in China included plans producing milk powder, ice cream, condensed milk, chocolate drinks and instant coffee.
"We expect Nestle's total investment in China to reach five billion yuan by the year 2000," Maucher said, adding that sales would double every two years.
Theo Klauser, chief executive of Nestle (China) Investment Services Ltd, said the two-year target for doubling sales would be ambitious and that three years might be more achievable.
